deep.reconstruction:
Setting: isotropic linear elasticity with Lamé constants λ, μ and displacement (u,v,w). The previous page uses N1 = λθ + 2μ u_x, T1 = μ(v_z + w_y), and so on, where θ = div(u,v,w). It also contains a reciprocity relation and a 4π u_0 point-source representation.

(1) First line. Riemann writes a minimum principle:
  ∫∫∫ dx dy dz [ (λ+2μ)(u_x+v_y+w_z)^2 + μ((u_y−v_x)^2 + (u_z−w_x)^2 + (v_z−w_y)^2) ] = min.
A small insertion over 'dx' is probably the factor (λ+2μ) on the θ² term; this reading is mine. In modern form the integrand is (λ+2μ)(div u)^2 + μ|curl u|^2.

(2) Second line. This is the boundary term from varying this functional, i.e. the coefficient of u in the surface integral after integration by parts:
  u[(λ+2μ)θ m + μ(u_y−v_x) n + μ(u_z−w_x) p].
Here m, n, p are the direction cosines of the outward normal. The μ is written only once, but it is clearly meant to multiply both curl terms.

(3) Next line, 'N1 ∂u/∂x + μ(Γ3²+Γ1²+Γ2²)'. My reading is that the usual quadratic form is written as 2W = Σ N_i e_ii + μ Σ (shear_i)². Riemann then expands it as
  2W = λ p² + 2μ(q1²+q2²+q3²) + μ(r1²+r2²+r3²),
with the labels written underneath:
  p = θ;
  q1 = u_x, q2 = v_y, q3 = w_z;
  r1 = v_z + w_y, r2 = w_x + u_z, r3 = u_y + v_x.
The implicit point, which I supply, is that the two integrands differ by
  4μ[(u_x v_y − u_y v_x) + (v_y w_z − v_z w_y) + (w_z u_x − w_x u_z)].
This is a sum of 2×2 Jacobians, i.e. a null Lagrangian (a divergence). So both functionals give the same interior Euler–Lagrange equations (Navier's equations); only the boundary terms differ.

(4) Euler–Lagrange (volume) terms. The coefficients of the variations u, v, w are:
  δu: λ p_x + 2μ q1_x + μ r3_y + μ r2_z;
  δv: λ p_y + 2μ q2_y + μ(r1_z + r3_x);
  δw: λ p_z + 2μ q3_z + μ(r2_x + r1_y).
These are exactly ∂N1/∂x + ∂T3/∂y + ∂T2/∂z and its cyclic analogues, i.e. the equilibrium equations (=0 without body force).

(5) Main new step. Riemann regards p, q_i, r_i as unknowns to be chosen so that these three expressions vanish identically, and introduces three potentials α, β, γ:
  r1 = α_yz, r2 = β_zx, r3 = γ_xy;
  2q1 = −γ_yy − β_zz − (λ/μ)p;
  2q2 = −α_zz − γ_xx − (λ/μ)p;
  2q3 = −β_xx − α_yy − (λ/μ)p.
In stress language:
  N1 = λp + 2μq1 = −μ(γ_yy + β_zz), T1 = μ r1 = μ α_yz, cyclically.
Then
  ∂N1/∂x + ∂T3/∂y + ∂T2/∂z = μ(−γ_yyx − β_zzx + γ_xyy + β_zxz) = 0,
and likewise for the other two. Equilibrium therefore holds identically for arbitrary α, β, γ. This is precisely Maxwell's three-function representation of a self-equilibrated stress field, up to an overall sign and the factor μ. A crossed-out first attempt (r3 = ∂α1/∂z, r2 = −∂α1/∂y) used first-order potentials instead.

(6) Bottom four lines, in faint ink. They read roughly:
  α ~ −∫v dy − ∫w dz;
  β ~ −∫w dz − ∫u dx;
  γ ~ −∫u dx − ∫v dy;
  p ~ u_x + v_y + w_z.
The German word is uncertain ('ausgedrückt in' or similar). These appear to be a heuristic correspondence between the stress potentials and displacement integrals. For example, α_yz = −(v_z + w_y) = −r1 under this correspondence, which suggests a duality between the stress-function (equilibrium) representation and the strain–displacement relations. The page does not develop it further.
errors: Line 2: the factor μ is written only before the first curl term; it should multiply (u_z − w_x)p as well. This is a notational omission.

The 2q3 line in the image appears to read −∂²β/∂y² (and 2q2 has ∂α/∂z² without the exponent). Consistency with the cyclic pattern and with the equilibrium identity requires −∂²β/∂x² − ∂²α/∂y². These are slips of the pen.

If (λ+2μ) is not in fact written on the θ² term in line 1, the functional would have coefficient 1 there and would not be equivalent to the elastic energy. The image suggests the factor is inserted above 'dx'.

The page does not address completeness: whether every equilibrated stress field has this form, or compatibility (that the resulting strains derive from a displacement). Neither is claimed, so this is incompleteness rather than an error.
The bottom correspondences α ↔ −∫v dy − ∫w dz etc. are heuristic and only partially consistent: α_yz gives −r1, but γ_yy + β_zz does not give a clean multiple of q1.

results.what: Elastic energy written as (λ+2μ)(div u)^2 + μ|curl u|^2, equivalent modulo a null Lagrangian to λθ² + 2μΣe_ii² + μΣγ_ij², with the same Navier Euler–Lagrange equations and the natural boundary terms.
results.modern_name: Div–curl form of the isotropic strain energy; null-Lagrangian equivalence
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Navier, Cauchy, Green, Kirchhoff; standard by the mid-19th century)

results.what: Equilibrium (Navier) equations written in terms of p = θ, q_i = normal strains, r_i = engineering shear strains.
Representation N1 = −μ(γ_yy + β_zz), T1 = μ α_yz (cyclic), which satisfies the homogeneous equilibrium equations identically for arbitrary α, β, γ.
results.modern_name: Maxwell stress functions (3D generalization of the Airy stress function; special case of the Beltrami/Morera stress function tensor)
results.usually_credited_to: J. C. Maxwell (1868/1870, 'On reciprocal figures...'); Airy (1862–63) in 2D; Morera (1892); Beltrami (1892)

results.what: Heuristic pairing of the stress potentials α, β, γ with integrals of the displacement components, and of p with the divergence.
results.modern_name: Duality between equilibrium (stress functions) and kinematic compatibility (strain–displacement)
results.usually_credited_to: unsure (later 19th–20th c. elasticity duality; e.g. Southwell's static–geometric analogy for shells)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a correct, explicit three-potential representation of self-equilibrated 3D stress fields, of Maxwell's type. In the literature this is credited to Maxwell (1868–70), following Airy's 2D function (1862), with Morera and Beltrami generalizing in 1892. Riemann is not known for work in elasticity, and if the page predates 1868 it anticipates Maxwell's stress functions. The date is uncertain: the bundle label 1853 is not a reliable date for the leaf, and the page is a brief, undeveloped sketch. The rest of the page is routine variational elasticity. That puts it at a notable unpublished detail rather than a major priority claim.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; x,y,z,mu=symbols('x y z mu'); a=Function('a')(x,y,z); b=Function('b')(x,y,z); g=Function('g')(x,y,z); N1=-mu*(diff(g,y,2)+diff(b,z,2)); N2=-mu*(diff(a,z,2)+diff(g,x,2)); N3=-mu*(diff(b,x,2)+diff(a,y,2)); T1=mu*diff(a,y,z); T2=mu*diff(b,z,x); T3=mu*diff(g,x,y); [simplify(diff(N1,x)+diff(T3,y)+diff(T2,z)), simplify(diff(T3,x)+diff(N2,y)+diff(T1,z)), simplify(diff(T2,x)+diff(T1,y)+diff(N3,z))]
checkable.asserts: All three equilibrium equations vanish identically for arbitrary α, β, γ (expected [0,0,0]).

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; x,y,z,lam,mu=symbols('x y z lam mu'); u,v,w=[Function(n)(x,y,z) for n in 'uvw']; th=diff(u,x)+diff(v,y)+diff(w,z); E1=(lam+2*mu)*th**2+mu*((diff(u,y)-diff(v,x))**2+(diff(u,z)-diff(w,x))**2+(diff(v,z)-diff(w,y))**2); E2=lam*th**2+2*mu*(diff(u,x)**2+diff(v,y)**2+diff(w,z)**2)+mu*((diff(v,z)+diff(w,y))**2+(diff(w,x)+diff(u,z))**2+(diff(u,y)+diff(v,x))**2); expand(E1-E2-4*mu*((diff(u,x)*diff(v,y)-diff(u,y)*diff(v,x))+(diff(v,y)*diff(w,z)-diff(v,z)*diff(w,y))+(diff(w,z)*diff(u,x)-diff(w,x)*diff(u,z))))
checkable.asserts: The two energy densities differ exactly by 4μ times a sum of 2×2 Jacobians (expected 0).

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; from sympy.calculus.euler import euler_equations; x,y,z,lam,mu=symbols('x y z lam mu'); u,v,w=[Function(n)(x,y,z) for n in 'uvw']; th=diff(u,x)+diff(v,y)+diff(w,z); J=(diff(u,x)*diff(v,y)-diff(u,y)*diff(v,x))+(diff(v,y)*diff(w,z)-diff(v,z)*diff(w,y))+(diff(w,z)*diff(u,x)-diff(w,x)*diff(u,z)); [simplify(e.lhs) for e in euler_equations(J,[u,v,w],[x,y,z])]
checkable.asserts: The Jacobian sum is a null Lagrangian: its Euler–Lagrange expressions vanish identically (expected [0,0,0]).

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; x,y,z,lam,mu=symbols('x y z lam mu'); u,v,w=[Function(n)(x,y,z) for n in 'uvw']; p=diff(u,x)+diff(v,y)+diff(w,z); q1=diff(u,x); r2=diff(w,x)+diff(u,z); r3=diff(u,y)+diff(v,x); simplify(lam*diff(p,x)+2*mu*diff(q1,x)+mu*diff(r3,y)+mu*diff(r2,z)-((lam+mu)*diff(p,x)+mu*(diff(u,x,2)+diff(u,y,2)+diff(u,z,2))))
checkable.asserts: Riemann's u-coefficient equals the Navier operator (λ+μ)∂θ/∂x + μΔu (expected 0).

transcription_corrections: First line: the integrand's θ² term appears to carry an inserted factor (λ+2μ), written small above 'dx'.
Line 2: the factor μ should apply to the second curl term (u_z−w_x)p too; the m, n, p here are direction cosines, not the p = θ defined later.
Third line: 'Γ_3^2+Γ_1^2+Γ_2^2' likely denotes the squared shear strains (r_3, r_1, r_2 in later notation), and 'N_1 ∂u/∂x' stands for the sum Σ N_i e_ii; the reading is uncertain.
2q_2 line: the image shows −∂α/∂z² (exponent omitted); intended −∂²α/∂z².
2q_3 line: the first term in the image looks like −∂²β/∂y²; the consistent form is −∂²β/∂x².
Bottom four lines: the German word read as 'ausgedrückt' is uncertain (possibly 'entspricht' or 'aufgefasst als'); the lines state a correspondence, not an equation.
